assessment.summary: Four independent trust-boundary failures are best addressed by small local controls rather than a new security subsystem.

nonNegotiables: Preserve user-approved code transfer, editing, command execution, and endpoints.
Do not add a URL allowlist, database, credential service, proxy, task namespace, or policy engine.
Use focused test-first changes and independent QA after each major milestone.
Emit troubleshooting logs without prompts, source, responses, redirect locations, or credential values.
Update documentation and the authorized Codex memory note only after verified behavior exists.
assumptions: The product remains single-user and all projects share task history.
MCP roots are informational and cannot alone prove filesystem enforcement.
Keyed Claude tool availability is restricted by its CLI arguments; Gemini and Claude writable-mode contracts require later runtime verification.

openQuestions: Do the installed Gemini and Claude CLIs expose native writable modes that remain confined to the approved working directory?
Does the calling Codex host apply an inherited OS sandbox to the MCP server and its child processes?
